targetedParagraphRepairs.before: This explanation teaches disease mechanisms and observation/reporting boundaries. Tell healthcare professionals the observation time, personal words, differences from usual and actions taken. It does not authorize diagnosis or treatment changes.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: This explanation teaches how diseases arise and the boundaries of observation and reporting. Tell healthcare professionals when you made the observation, what the person said, how the situation differs from usual and what action you took. This material does not provide instructions for diagnosis or changes to treatment.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Nerve damage can reduce sensation so wounds may cause little pain. Persistent high glucose can also delay healing. The person’s no-pain statement matters, but differs from proof of no wound or safety.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: If nerve damage reduces sensation, a person may feel little pain even when they have a wound. Persistent high blood glucose may also make wounds slower to heal. The person’s statement that they do not feel pain is important information, but it is separate from evidence that there is no wound or that the situation is safe.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: If a wound, redness or skin breakdown is found, report location, appearance, sensation and noticing time according to the facility plan. Do not omit records because pain is absent or independently apply medication and obscure the course.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: If you find a wound, redness, skin breakdown or a similar change, report its location, observed appearance, the person’s sensation and the time you noticed it according to the facility’s plan. Do not omit the record because there is no pain, or independently apply medication and obscure how the condition develops.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Stoma appliances and waste handling follow the personal plan and necessary training. Report surrounding redness, skin breakdown, leaks or changes from usual. Inexperienced workers must not improvise appliance or opening adjustments.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Handle stoma appliances and excreted material according to the person’s plan and the necessary training. Report redness or skin breakdown around the stoma, leaks and changes from usual. A worker without the relevant experience must not improvise adjustments to the appliance or opening.
